image_description: A close-up view of a grey whale's head and rostrum emerging vertically from blue ocean water (spyhopping behavior). The skin is dark grey/black with distinctive mottled white patches caused by barnacles and cyamids. The rostrum is arched, and the two blowholes are visible at the top. The rest of the body, flippers, and tail are submerged or out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows the characteristic arched rostrum and the pair of blowholes at the apex of the head, matching the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture exhibits the correct high-contrast mottling pattern with white callosities/barnacle clusters typical of grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The posterior back and dorsal area are not visible in this vertical head-shot composition; therefore, the presence of knuckles cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head and upper neck are visible; the full body shape is occluded by water and framing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Visible skin on the head confirms the correct mottled pattern and coloration.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed, and the interior oral cavity containing baleen plates is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are submerged and not visible in the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely out of frame/submerged.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: High-resolution details on the snout show the rough, uneven texture associated with callosities and barnacle attachments.

The background water ripples appear somewhat uniform and repetitive, lacking the natural random variation of open ocean swells, suggesting potential pattern repetition or generative smoothing.
